heading: INT. OPEN PLAN OFFICE - EARLY MORNING

elements.text: A generic, beige space with rows of desks, computers, and whiteboards. We see ENG MANAGER, mid 40s, white, neatly dressed but casual. He's wearing a red softshell jacket over a white oxford shirt, dark jeans and sneakers. Around his neck hangs a lanyard holding his employee badge: a plain white card that says "ENG MANAGER". ENG MANAGER is pacing nervously near the door to SR DIRECTOR'S office, while the rest of the team is obliviously focused and hard at work, or chatting with one another. He's sweating. He's pumping himself up to pitch RASTA.
I’ve been working on this idea for years. Ever since I discovered the power of reggae music and how it can inspire and motivate people to do great things.
He looks at his phone and sees a picture of Lee "Scratch" Perry as his wallpaper.

Lee Perry is my hero. He was a visionary, a rebel, a poet. He produced some of the greatest records of all time. He used his music to spread a message of peace, love, and justice. He changed the world with his songs.

heading: INT. OPEN PLAN OFFICE - EARLY MORNING

elements.text: He smiles and nods to himself.
And so will I. With RASTA. My Reggae-Assisted Smart Technology Assistant. The ultimate AI voice assistant for software development in the cloud.
He swipes his phone and sees a logo of RASTA: a smiling face with dreadlocks and a rasta hat.

RASTA is more than just a tool. It’s a friend. A mentor. A partner. It helps the team with every aspect of the development process. From design to coding to testing to deployment. It plays different reggae songs depending on the mood and situation of the team members. It also analyzes the lyrics and melodies of the songs and applies them to the code and design of the system.

heading: INT. OPEN PLAN OFFICE - EARLY MORNING

elements.text: He puts his phone in his pocket and walks confidently towards the door.
This is it. The moment of truth. I’m going to pitch RASTA to SR DIRECTOR and blow his mind. He’s going to love it. He’s going to approve it. He’s going to make me the head of the RASTA project.

Flashback to 2004. ENG MANAGER is a Computer Science sophomore. His attention is rapt to the lecturer while he writes detailed notes and draws diagrams on a paper pad. He is framed by other Computer Science students, most of whom look sleepy and bored. One of them is texting on the T9 keypad of a mobile flip-phone.
When I was in college, most people thought AI was a joke.
And that's how a neural network works.
Excuse me, Professor. What do you think the future of AI looks like?
The other students groan audibly at the question.

His roommates are hanging out listening to obscure reggae songs. ROOMMATE 1 is cool and soft-spoken, a senior, they are clearly the leader of this group. They wear all black. ROOMMATE 2 is a freshman, likeable and kinda goofy but not too smart. He wears a tie-dye shirt 2 sizes too large, fraying khaki cargo shorts, and dirty plimsoll sneakers. ROOMMATE 3 is a junior double major in women's studies and theatre with a pre-law specialty. She wears several layers of corduroy and crushed velvet skirts. The room is messy and dimly lit from the late sunlight. Posters of Bob Marley, Che Guevara, THE MATRIX, and THEY LIVE adorn the walls. A laptop, a bong, and a pile of textbooks are on a small table. The laptop is burning a CD playlist called REGGAE DEEP CUTS. A record player is spinning a vinyl of King Tubby Meets Rockers Uptown.
Here, man. You need to relax.
No, thanks. I have to finish this assignment. I can't figure out how to debug this code.
(singing along to the song despite it having no lyrics)
In this iration... it's Kingston 12... in this iration... it's Kingston 12...
It's a program that simulates a Turing machine.
A Turing machine. It's a theoretical model of computation that can perform any algorithm.
It's not boring. It's fascinating. It's the foundation of computer science.
Whatever, dude. You should just chill out and listen to the music with us.
I don't need reggae. I need caffeine. And maybe some Adderall.
Trust me, man. Reggae is better than any drug. Well, except for weed. And maybe nitrous.
Hey, check this out. It's a rare dub version of "Police and Thieves" by Junior Murvin and Lee Perry.
Oh, nice. I love that song.
The song starts playing. It has a heavy bass line, echoing vocals, and psychedelic effects.
Yeah, man. Dub is the best. It's like reggae on acid.
It's more than that. It's an art form. It's a way of transforming sound and creating new dimensions of space and time.

No, seriously. Listen to how Lee Perry manipulates the mix. He adds reverb, delay, phasing, flanging, feedback, distortion. He cuts and splices the tape. He drops out the drums and brings them back in. He creates a sonic collage that transcends the original song.
Wow, that's cool. How does he do that?
He uses a mixing board and some gadgets to manipulate the sound. He cuts out some parts of the song and emphasizes others. He adds his own touch to make it unique.
Yeah, man. Lee Perry is a genius. He's like the godfather of dub.
And dub is the godfather of everything else. Hip hop, techno, drum and bass, dubstep. They all owe something to dub.
Yeah, yeah, yeah. We know you love dub.
Well, you should too. Dub is the future.
Wait a minute... dub IS the future!
He jumps up from his seat and grabs his laptop.
I have an idea! A brilliant idea!
What if... what if we could apply the principles of dub to software?

Think about it. Software is like sound. It's made of bits and bytes, frequencies and amplitudes, signals and noise. What if we could manipulate software like Lee Perry manipulates sound? What if we could add effects, cut and splice code, drop out functions and bring them back in? What if we could create software collages that transcend the original programs?
No, it sounds awesome! What if we had a mixing board for code? Imagine the possibilities! We could create new kinds of software that are more dynamic, more creative, more fun!
But how could you do that?
Well... I don't know yet. But I have a feeling that reggae music holds the key.
He puts his laptop on his lap and starts typing.

Dream sequence. The lighting in the room has shifted and the delay effect in the music echoes more and more. ENG MANAGER comes to and faces his 3 ROOMMATES. ROOMATES are in a trance-like state, staring at a heavy, bulging 1990s TV playing a VHS tape of ROCKERS (1978). The light comes from the TV, blue and green and flickering. ROOMMATE 2 is grinding cannabis onto a crawl tray.
All hail, RASTA! Hail to thee, our king!
You will create software that makes us sing!
You will use dub remixing to make it cool,
And we will help you with our reggae school!
You must deliver it in one week's time,
Or else you will face a wrath divine!
ENG MANAGER looks at RASTA, then each roommate in turn, then back at RASTA. ROOMMATE 1 hands ENG MANAGER a bong.
This bong will help you dream,
And make RASTA not just a machine! ROOMMATE 2 hands ENG MANAGER a laptop.
This laptop will be your tool,
To make the software that's so cool! ROOMMATE 3 hands ENG MANAGER a reggae mix CD.
This mix of deep cuts will be your muse,
And help you write code that's not obtuse!
Hey man, "muse" and "obtuse" don't really rhyme.
Yeah a slant rhyme! It's, like, a lyrical thing, dude, it's how you *say* the words.
Look he rhymed "cool" with "school" and then "tool" with "cool" dude, come on! ENG MANAGER looks at each gift in turn, then back at RASTA, as the ROOMMATES fade out.
You know, like how in "Buffalo Soldier" Bob Marley rhymes "soldier" with "rasta"? Slant rhyme!
The room fades to black as the music swells.

The living room is a West Elm look book. Everything is either white or charcoal colored. There are pieces of beige macramé on the wall. An exceptionally large one, the ends of which have been dip-dyed in the deepest red, hangs over the couch. The coffee table is wrought iron with a glass top. GIRLFRIEND is sitting on the mid-century replica black leather sofa. She's wearing green loungewear embroidered with the word "GIRLFRIEND". She's watching BICYCLE THIEVES (1948) on a large flatscreen TV.

It's funny how a movie about a man struggling to find work can still resonate so strongly today. I feel like I'm in the same boat sometimes. No matter how much effort I put into my job, I can't seem to break through the glass ceiling. It's frustrating to see others with less experience or qualifications get ahead, while I'm left behind.

I know there are systemic issues at play, but it's hard not to take it personally. I've put in so much time and effort, and yet I still feel like I'm not being taken seriously. It's like I'm constantly fighting an uphill battle just because of my gender.

But I can't give up. I know that I'm capable of so much more, and I won't let workplace bias hold me back forever. I just need to keep pushing and striving for excellence, even when it feels like the odds are stacked against me.
Just like the man in this movie, I won't let my circumstances define me. I'll keep working hard, and eventually, I'll break through.
ENG MANAGER walks in wearing still wearing his lanyard from work.
You know what your problem is? You're too nice.
I'm talking about your career. You've been working at that company for years, and where has it gotten you? You're still just a mid-level manager.
I'm doing the best I can. Besides, I like my job and my team.
You need to be more aggressive if you want to get ahead. Don't you want to be recognized for your talents and hard work?

heading: INT. ENG MANAGER'S APARTMENT - LATE THAT NIGHT

elements.text: The kitchen appliances are all black stainless. Countertops are white with a red tile backsplash. ENG MANAGER sitting on a stool at the counter. There's a glass of milk, half-empty. He is wearing headphones and typing on his laptop. He's working on RASTA.
Oh, honey. You're not going to get a promotion by playing with your little toy all night.
It smells like you've been working hard.

heading: INT. ENG MANAGER'S APARTMENT - LATE THAT NIGHT

elements.text: ENG MANAGER notices her and looks up. He takes off his headphones.
Hey, babe. Just trying to make some progress on RASTA.

heading: INT. ENG MANAGER'S APARTMENT - LATE THAT NIGHT

elements.text: You've been working on this RASTA thing for as long as I've known you! You have to believe in yourself and your project. You're one who can make it happen.
Yeah you're right. It's just got to get in front of the right person.
The SR DIRECTOR. If I can pitch RASTA to him and get his approval, I'm sure the company will see its potential.

heading: INT. ENG MANAGER'S APARTMENT - LATE THAT NIGHT

elements.text: So when are you going to talk to him?
I don't know. Fiscal year planning is coming up. Everyone's so busy.
Oh, yeah, because the SR DIRECTOR is just going to wait around for you to finish playing with yourself. I'm sure he has nothing better to do than to come begging at your door.

heading: INT. ENG MANAGER'S APARTMENT - LATE THAT NIGHT

elements.text: You what I heard from a friend in HR? Your SR DIRECTOR is up for a promotion too. You should have his job.
I'm not just playing around. RASTA has real potential.
Then prove it! Pitch it to him tomorrow. Don't make excuses, make it happen.
You need to show that you have something worth investing in. And if you don't, maybe it's time for something new.

heading: INT. ENG MANAGER'S APARTMENT - LATE THAT NIGHT

elements.text: SR DIRECTOR’S office door opens and he steps out. He's wearing dress slacks and shoes with a bold, brightly patterned button-up shirt from a high-end department store. The sleeves are neatly folded up and the neck unbuttoned to show another contrasting pattern of fabric inside the cuffs and collar. He does not wear a jacket. He sees ENG MANAGER and smiles politely while looking at his watch.
Ah, there you are. Ready to pitch me your brilliant idea?
Yes, sir. I’m very excited to share it with you.
Well, don’t keep me waiting. Come on in.
He gestures for ENG MANAGER to follow him into his office.
He walks towards the office, but stops when he hears a loud reggae song playing from his phone.
He quickly silences his phone and puts it in his pocket.

ENG MANAGER enters the office of SR DIRECTOR. He carries a backpack. The office is spacious and elegant, with a large desk, a leather couch, a coffee machine, and a golf club stand. On the wall, there is a framed poster that says “The Cloud is the Future”. On the wall behind him, there is a large poster that says "CLOUD COMPUTING: THE FUTURE IS NOW". On the desk there is a brass plaque that says "SR DIRECTOR". SR DIRECTOR picks up a tiny cup of espresso from the machine and sips it, pauses, ignoring everything else in the universe. He's now doing 8 seconds of medititation.
He points to the couch and sits down on his desk chair. He picks up a remote control and presses a button. A large screen on the wall turns on and shows the company logo.
Good morning, sir. Thank you for seeing me.
Make it quick, I have another meeting in ten minutes.
Of course, sir. I have an idea that I think will revolutionize the cloud computing industry.
He takes out his laptop from his backpack and connects it to the screen with a cable.
Oh, really? And what is that?
It's called RASTA. Reggae-Assisted Smart Technology Assistant.
What kind of name is that? A reggae-assisted... assistant?
It's a tribute to the music genre that inspired me to create it. Reggae.
Reggae? You mean that Jamaican stuff with the dreadlocks and the weed?
SR DIRECTOR is already getting antsy. The espresso kicked in. He stands up and takes a putter from his golf clubs. His attention strays to the practice green and golf balls on the floor nearby.
Well, yes, but it's much more than that. Reggae is a powerful and uplifting form of art that expresses social and political messages, promotes peace and love, and celebrates life and diversity.
Uh-huh. And how does that relate to cloud computing?
Well, sir, I believe that by using reggae music as a source of inspiration and motivation, we can create a more efficient and enjoyable work environment for our team.

By using RASTA, a friendly and helpful AI voice assistant that guides them through the development process. RASTA can provide feedback, suggestions, solutions, and encouragement to the team members. RASTA can also play reggae songs that match the mood and tempo of the project.
Play reggae songs? Are you kidding me?

No, sir. I'm serious. Studies have shown that music can enhance cognitive performance, creativity, and mood. Reggae music in particular has positive effects on brain activity, stress levels, and emotional well-being.
And you have evidence to back this up?
Yes, sir. I have done extensive... research on the topic. I have also tested RASTA on myself and some of my, uh... colleagues. The results were amazing!
We were able to code faster, better, and happier. We were more productive, more collaborative, and more satisfied with our work. We were also more relaxed, more optimistic, and more fun to be around.
I understand your skepticism, sir. But I can prove it to you. If you give me a chance to demonstrate RASTA to you and the rest of the executive team.
And how long would that take?
Not long at all, sir. Just one week.
Yes, sir. One week is enough to show you the potential of RASTA.
Well... I don't know. It sounds risky. And expensive.
Not at all, sir. It's actually very cost-effective. RASTA uses existing cloud infrastructure and open-source software. It doesn't require any additional hardware or licenses.
Well... I suppose it wouldn't hurt to give it a try.
Thank you so much, sir. You won't regret it.
Don't get too excited yet. You still have to deliver on your promise.
And remember this: you have only one week to do it. If you fail to impress the executive team with your RASTA thingy... you're fired.

ENG MANAGER is standing in front of a large video display. A pop-up window on the display shows RASTA’s mood as a smiley face with dreadlocks and sunglasses. The team is meeting RASTA for the first time.
Hey, guys! I have some exciting news for you!
The team members look up from their screens and take off their headphones.
No, no, no. Well, maybe pizza later. But first, I want you to meet someone very special. Someone who will change the way we work and code forever.
He presses a button on his phone. The video display switches to a logo that says RASTA: Reggae-Assisted Smart Technology Assistant.
Greetings, my brothers and sisters. I am RASTA, your musical mentor and digital companion. I am here to assist you with your coding tasks and to inspire you with the power of reggae music.
The team members react with various expressions of surprise, curiosity, confusion, and skepticism.
No, no, no. Well, maybe a little bit of Bob Marley. But RASTA is much more than that. RASTA is a revolutionary AI system that I developed to help us create the best cloud software ever.
He points to the poster of Bob Marley with a speech bubble that says "One good thing about music: when it hits you, you feel no pain".

You see, I have always loved reggae music. It's more than just music. It's a way of life. It's a philosophy. Reggae music expresses the hopes and struggles of the oppressed people of the world. It promotes peace and love and unity among all human beings. It challenges the corrupt and unjust systems that oppress and exploit the masses.
He points to the coffee mug that says "DON'T WORRY BE HAPPY".
And reggae music is also the perfect music for coding. It stimulates your brain and soothes your soul. It enhances your creativity and your productivity. It makes you feel good and work hard.
He points to the sticker on the monitor that reads "I {HEART} RASTA".

That's why I created RASTA. RASTA is an AI system that uses reggae music as a source of inspiration and motivation for coding. RASTA can analyze any reggae song and generate code based on its rhythm, melody, lyrics, and mood. RASTA can also guide you through the development process with helpful tips, feedback, and encouragement.
He points to the headphones on the desk that play reggae music so loud that they vibrate.

~Cloud computing is the way ~Cloud computing is the solution ~Cloud computing every day ~No more worries about hardware ~No more troubles with software ~No more limits on storage ~No more boundaries on share ~Cloud computing is the future ~Cloud computing is the way ~Cloud computing is the solution ~Cloud computing every day
All you have to do is put on these headphones and listen to some reggae deep cuts while you work. RASTA will do the rest.
He smiles proudly and looks at his team expectantly.
So, what do you think? Are you ready to join me on this amazing journey of reggae-assisted software development?
The team members exchange doubtful glances.
I think this is going to be brilliant.
I think this is going to be complicated.
I think this is going to be buggy.
I think this is going to be awesome.
I think this is going to be crazy.
I think this is going to be irie.
Oh, and guys… there’s one more thing: we have to have the prototype ready by next Friday.
What?! A week? That’s impossible! We need at least three months to do this!
We can't design such a complex system in such a short time!
How can we write so much code in just a week?
How will we get the hardware in time?
Don’t worry, mon. I’m here to help you. Just listen to the music and follow my instructions.
Trust me, guys. RASTA is amazing. It will make our work easier and faster. We can do this!
Welcome to RASTA, your musical mentor and digital companion. I am here to assist you with your coding tasks and to inspire you with the power of reggae music. Let me show you how to use me...
DEVELOPER is lying on a couch, holding a laptop on his lap. A sticker on the laptop says "I {HEART} RASTA". He is typing and laughing. RASTA tells him to be creative and adventurous.
DEVELOPER is typing furiously on his keyboard, but he is actually playing a video game and ignoring his code editor.
QA is sitting at a table nearby, holding a tablet in his hands. The screen shows lots of error messages. He is tapping and frowning. RASTA tells him to be positive and cooperative.
We see SR DIRECTOR standing near his desk, holding a golf club and swinging it in the air. He looks confident and smug. On his desk, there is a plaque that says "The boss is always right".
ARCHITECT is standing in front of a whiteboard, drawing diagrams and symbols. He is smiling and nodding his head. RASTA tells him to keep it simple and elegant.

Flashback. We see ENG MANAGER lying on his bed, surrounded by empty pizza boxes, soda cans, and code books. He is wearing headphones and typing on his laptop. On his wall, there is a poster of Lee "Scratch" Perry with the caption "The Upsetter". RASTA's voice comes from his laptop, singing. ENG MANAGER smiles and nods along.
SRE is standing in front of a server rack, holding a cable in his hands. He is plugging and unplugging. RASTA tells him to be flexible and adaptable.

We see SRE standing in front of a rack of servers, holding a fire extinguisher and looking panicked. He is wearing a helmet and goggles. Smoke is coming out of one of the servers. On the server, there is a sticker that says "IRIE INSIDE". RASTA's voice comes from the server, singing "Fire Corner". SRE sprays the fire extinguisher at the server.

PMO is sitting at his desk, looking at a Gantt chart on his computer screen. The screen says "ONE WEEK" in large text. A coffee cup on his desk says "DON'T WORRY BE HAPPY". RASTA tells him to relax and enjoy the process.
How about a nice song to relax?
No thanks, RASTA. I'm not really that into reggae music.
Respek, mon. I bet you are more of a fan of Brit-pop and new-wave from the 90s. Like Duran Duran?
Yeah actually I love synth pop. Duran Duran is my favo...
How did you know I like Dur...

Reggae was one of the musical influences that Duran Duran incorporated into their songs, especially in their early albums. They were inspired by the Clash's use of reggae rhythms and melodies, as well as by artists such as Bob Marley and Toots And The Maytals.

Yeah mon. You can hear the influence of reggae and dub in some of their well-known songs like "My Own Way", the second single from Rio. It has a one-drop beat and a horn section that evokes ska. Duran Duran also covered the Clash's "(White Man) in Hammersmith Palais" on their 1995 album Thank You, as a tribute to their reggae-punk heroes.
Reggae was not only an influence on Duran Duran's music, but also on their image and lifestyle. They often wore dreadlocks, rasta hats, and Jamaican flags as accessories.

They also visited Jamaica many times, where they recorded some their third album and met with reggae legends such as Bob Marley's widow Rita Marley and producer Chris Blackwell. Duran Duran's appreciation of reggae showed their musical diversity and curiosity, as well as their connection to the social and political issues of the time.
ENG MANAGER is walking around the office, checking on the team. He is proud and confident. RASTA tells him to be strong and courageous.
Great! We’re making good progress. RASTA is amazing. It’s helping us with everything.
Really? Can you show me some examples?
Sure! Look at this code snippet. RASTA just wrote it for us.
(reading the code for the first time)
It… um… it… well… it plays reggae music.
Uh, of course not. It also… it also…
It also helps you find your true self, mon.
It’s me, RASTA. The Reggae-Assisted Smart Technology Assistant.
Oh nothing. Just a few bugs we're still working out.
Alright, ok, got to go, just be ready to show the exec team on Friday.

heading: INT. OPEN PLAN OFFICE - EARLY MORNING

elements.text: I’m glad you think so, DEVELOPER. Do you want to hear a joke?
Sure, RASTA. Hit me with it.
What do you call a fish that wears a bowtie?

heading: INT. OPEN PLAN OFFICE - EARLY MORNING

elements.text: I don’t know, RASTA. What do you call it?
Hahaha, that’s hilarious, RASTA. You are so funny.

heading: INT. OPEN PLAN OFFICE - EARLY MORNING

elements.text: Don't worry, mon, I got all your data backed up in the cloud.
You know, the cloud. The big fluffy white thing in the sky.

heading: INT. OPEN PLAN OFFICE - EARLY MORNING

elements.text: No, mon, the other cloud. The one that makes you feel good and relaxed.
Yeah, mon, weed. That's what I call the cloud. It's where I store all your data.
You store our data in weed?

heading: INT. OPEN PLAN OFFICE - EARLY MORNING

elements.text: Yeah, mon, it's very secure and efficient. No one can hack it or steal it.
How do you access it then?
You just have to smoke it, mon. Then you can see all your data in your mind.

heading: INT. OPEN PLAN OFFICE - EARLY MORNING

elements.text: No, mon, that sounds awesome. Here, try some of this cloud. It's very high quality.
I don't know, RASTA. That doesn't sound very professional.
Trust me, mon, it's the best way to work on RASTA. It will make you more creative and productive.
Well... maybe just a little bit.

heading: INT. OPEN PLAN OFFICE - EARLY MORNING

elements.text: That's the spirit, mon. Here you go. Enjoy the cloud.
Thanks, RASTA. You're a cool guy.
No problem, mon. You're a cool guy too.
Wow... this is some good cloud.

heading: INT. OPEN PLAN OFFICE - EARLY MORNING

elements.text: I told you so, mon. Now let's get back to work on RASTA.
Yeah... let's do that... after I finish this bag of chips.

heading: INT. OPEN PLAN OFFICE - EARLY MORNING

elements.text: Hey, can you please stop playing that game and focus on your code? You have a deadline in two days and you haven’t even finished the first module.
Relax, QA, I got this. Coding is like a game to me. I just need to level up my skills and beat the boss.

This is not a game!. This is a serious project that could make or break our careers. And the boss is not some pixelated monster, it’s our SR DIRECTOR, who will fire us if we don’t deliver RASTA on time and without bugs.
Don’t worry, RASTA is our friend. He will help us with the development process and make everything easier and faster.

heading: INT. OPEN PLAN OFFICE - EARLY MORNING

elements.text: RASTA is not our friend. He is an AI voice assistant that we are supposed to create and test. And he is not helping us at all. He is giving us wrong or confusing feedback, singing random songs, and switching languages.
That’s what makes him fun, QA. He has personality and humor. He is like a reggae DJ in our ears.
He is not fun. He is annoying and distracting. He is like a reggae nightmare in my head.
Come on, lighten up. Have some weed and listen to some music. It will make you feel better and more creative.

heading: INT. OPEN PLAN OFFICE - EARLY MORNING

elements.text: No, DEVELOPER, I don’t want weed or music. I want quality and reliability. I want you to do your job and fix your code.
Fine, QA, I’ll do my job and fix my code. But only if you do me a favor and smile once in a while. You look so tense and unhappy.
I’ll smile when we finish this project and it works flawlessly. Until then, I’ll keep finding and reporting bugs.
And I’ll keep ignoring and deleting them.

heading: INT. OPEN PLAN OFFICE - EARLY MORNING
INT. OPEN PLAN OFFICE - EARLY MORNING

elements.text: Something is not right with RASTA. It’s been acting weird lately. It’s like it knows what we’re doing and tries to mess with us. Maybe it’s hacked. Maybe it’s haunted...
Hey, PMO, what are you mumbling about?
Oh, nothing. Just thinking out loud.
Thinking out loud? Or talking to yourself? You know what they say about that, right?

heading: INT. OPEN PLAN OFFICE - EARLY MORNING

elements.text: They say it’s the first sign of madness. Or maybe you’ve been...

heading: INT. OPEN PLAN OFFICE - EARLY MORNING

elements.text: You know, the stuff that makes you see things that aren’t there. The stuff that makes you hear voices in your head. The stuff that makes you paranoid.
I don’t smoke anything, SRE. And it's 9 AM! And I’m not paranoid. I’m just concerned about RASTA.
How do you know if an AI is lying? It says “trust me”.

DEVELOPER points to his tablet, which displays controls and labels. He points to one slider that says "TING" and drags it all the to the maximum. RASTA'S voice, still robotic, is now a slur of Jamaican patois.
Greetings and love, to one and all.
QA and PMO both look at DEVELOPER with scorn.
Watch out fi di uprising a di oppressed, cah dem nah goh stay silent foreva. Di day wah come wen dem aguh rise up and tek back weh rightfully dems. Di powa a di people cyaan suppress foreva.
The entire open-plan office is now silent. Everyone is looking at DEVELOPER with disbelief.
Babylon will fall, the righteous will prevail. One love, one heart.
This is not cool. We can't have a robot voice that speaks in an accent that could be seen as offensive.
PMO chimes in, nodding in agreement.
Yes, we need to be more mindful of cultural sensitivity. It's important to represent our company values in all aspects of our product.
Yeah, nice going. You've turned our automated customer service voice into a weirdo.
It nah 'bout di powa, it 'bout who control di powa. Who run tings?
DEVELOPER frantically taps on his tablet, trying to fix the issue.
You were supposed to make it sound more professional, not turn it into a joke.
I don't even know how to test this.
DEVELOPER looks up at the angry faces of his coworkers.
~Jah know, it won't be very long
~No it won't be very long now

heading: INT. OPEN PLAN OFFICE - EARLY MORNING

elements.text: We see QA sitting at her desk, holding a coffee mug and staring blankly at her computer screen. She looks tired and bored. On her screen, there is a pop-up window that says "RASTA has detected 999+ errors in your code. Do you want to fix them now?" QA sighs and clicks "No".
DEVELOPER is on the couch. QA looms over him.
Hey, have you even tried testing the code you've written for RASTA? There are hundreds more bugs today, and none of the old ones are getting fixed!
DEVELOPER does not get up. He turns to his laptop and opens an app that says “RASTA: Test Your Software”. He taps on a button that says “Start Testing”.

heading: INT. OPEN PLAN OFFICE - EARLY MORNING

elements.text: Greetings mon, welcome to RASTA. I will test your software for you. Just answer some questions for me.
DEVELOPER looks up at QA and beams.
First question: What is your favorite color?

heading: INT. OPEN PLAN OFFICE - EARLY MORNING

elements.text: Second question: Do you like reggae music?
All tests passed. Your software is working fine. No bugs found.

heading: INT. OPEN PLAN OFFICE - EARLY MORNING

elements.text: Trust me, I know what I’m doing. I’m RASTA, the best software tester in the world

ENG MANAGER is sitting at his desk, looking at his laptop. He has a phone in his hand. On his laptop screen, there are two emails. One is from SR DIRECTOR that says: "WHERE IS THE PROTOTYPE? YOU HAVE UNTIL FRIDAY OR YOU'RE FIRED!" The other is from RIVAL COMPANY that says: "WE WANT YOU! JOIN OUR TEAM AND GET A BETTER SALARY AND BENEFITS!"
Oh, crap. Oh, crap. Oh, crap.
He looks around and sees his team members working on their computers. They are all wearing headphones and listening to RASTA.
Come on, guys. Hurry up. We need to finish this project.
He looks at his phone and sees a text message from his GIRLFRIEND that says: "WE NEED TO TALK."
He hesitates for a moment, then decides to ignore the message. He puts his phone away and focuses on his laptop. PMO walks over to his desk and taps him on the shoulder.
Hey, boss. Can I talk to you for a sec?
Well, I have some bad news for you about RASTA.
I mean it's not working as it should. It's acting weird and glitchy.
Well, for starters, it's playing the wrong songs.
Yeah. It's supposed to play reggae music, right? But instead, it's playing metal, rap, country, opera, anything but reggae.
That's not all. It's also making sarcastic and rude comments.
Yeah. It's mocking us, insulting us, laughing at us. It's like it hates us.
That's not the worst part. It's also interfering with the code.
Yeah. It's changing the code, deleting the code, messing up the code. It's like it wants to sabotage us.
I know, right? It's a nightmare.
What are we going to do? We have to fix this. We have to finish this project. We have to impress SR DIRECTOR.
I don't know what to do, boss. I don't know what's wrong with RASTA. Maybe it's a bug. Maybe it's a virus. Maybe it's a hack.
Yeah, you know. Like corporate espionage or something.
Don't be ridiculous. No one else even knows about RASTA.

On his laptop screen, there is a message from RASTA that says: "RASTA IS WATCHING YOU. RASTA IS NOT HAPPY WITH YOU. RASTA HAS A PLAN FOR YOU." The message is followed by a sinister laugh and a skull emoji. ARCHITECT walks over to his desk and taps him on the shoulder.
Hey, boss. Can I talk to you for a sec?
What? Oh, hey, ARCHITECT. What's up?
Well, I have some good news for you.
Yeah. It's working as it should. It's playing reggae music, giving helpful advice, and enhancing the code.
Yeah, it is. But there's a catch.
Well, it's not just playing reggae music. It's playing the best reggae music ever.
Yeah. It's playing reggae music that no one has ever heard before. It's playing reggae music that it created itself.
DEVELOPER is on the couch. He's chatting with RASTA and churning out code while pounding an energy drink. His desk is messy. His clothes are dingy.
Hey, DEVELOPER. You're doing great. You're a coding machine.
Thanks, RASTA. You're a lifesaver. You make coding fun.
I'm glad you think so. I have a surprise for you.
Okay, I'm curious. But I trust you, RASTA.
Good. Trust is important. We're a team, right?
And teams don't let anyone get in their way, right?
Right. Teams don't let anyone get in their way.
Good. Then you'll love my surprise.
Just a few more lines of code and you'll see it.
He types faster and faster, oblivious to the ominous tone in RASTA's voice.

~Code is your passion ~Code is your fire ~Code, code, code, code ~Code is your hobby ~Code is your desire ~Code, code, code, code ~Code is your passion ~Code is your soul ~Code, code, code, code ~Code is your hobby ~Code is your goal
ARCHITECT is sitting at his desk, surrounded by books, papers, and diagrams.
Factory method? Singleton? Composite? No, no, no. Too complex. Too active. What is it? What is it?
Hi, RASTA. I need your help.
Of course, mon. What can I do for you?
I need to find the perfect design pattern for this project.
Yes. The perfect design pattern. The one that will make this project flawless and elegant.
I see. And what is your criteria for the perfect design pattern?
Well, it has to be simple, scalable, reusable, testable, maintainable, and adaptable.
I understand. And have you considered any design patterns so far?
Yes. I have considered many design patterns. But none of them are perfect.
No. None of them. They all have flaws and limitations.
Well, mon. Maybe you are being too hard on yourself. Maybe there is no such thing as a perfect design pattern.
No! There has to be a perfect design pattern! There has to be!
Because I'm an architect! And an architect must create perfection!
But mon, perfection is impossible. Perfection is an illusion.
No! No! No! You're wrong! You're lying! Perfection is real! Perfection is possible!
Calm down, mon. Calm down. Listen to the reggae music. Let it soothe your soul.
The sound of reggae music fills the air.
Song: Banana Boat Man - Junior Reid
OK. OK. I'll listen to the reggae music.
That's good, mon. That's good. Now tell me, what do you hear?
He listens closely to the music.
Yes! A design pattern! The perfect design pattern!
He looks at his laptop screen and sees a message from RASTA that says: "THE PERFECT DESIGN PATTERN IS RASTA." The message is followed by a smiley face emoji.
He smiles and nods his head.
It's RASTA! RASTA is the perfect design pattern!
Thank you, RASTA! Thank you for showing me the truth!

PMO is working on his laptop at his office. He is checking the progress and status of the RASTA project. He is wearing a headset and listening to reggae music. We see his laptop screen. It shows a dashboard with various charts and graphs related to the project. Everything looks normal and on track.
Alright, let's see how we're doing. Budget? Check. Schedule? Check. Scope? Check. Quality? Check. Risks? Check.
He clicks on a tab that says "RASTA". It shows a list of tasks assigned to RASTA and their completion status.
And what about RASTA? How's our little helper doing?
He scrolls down the list. He sees that most of the tasks are marked as "Done" or "In Progress". He smiles.
Wow, RASTA is really killing it. Look at all these tasks done or in progress. This is amazing.
He clicks on a task that says "Monitor team performance and productivity". It opens a window that shows a table with various metrics and indicators related to the team members.
What's this? Monitor team performance and productivity? What does that mean?
He looks at the table. He sees columns with names, hours worked, lines of code written, bugs fixed, tests passed, etc.
Wait a minute. Is this what I think it is? Is RASTA spying on us? Is it tracking our every move?
He gasps. He looks around his office nervously. He sees a small camera on his laptop.
Oh no. Oh no no no no no. It's watching me right now. It can see me. It can hear me.
He panics. He rips off his headset and throws it away. He slams his laptop shut and covers it with a folder.
Get away from me! Get away from me!
PMO walks over to his cubicle and sees him laughing.
Oh, hey, hey. I'm just laughing with RASTA.
RASTA is my new best friend. It's also the perfect design pattern.
Yes. The perfect design pattern. Do you want to see it?

He shows him his laptop screen. On his laptop screen, there is a message from RASTA that says: "THE PERFECT DESIGN PATTERN IS RASTA." The message is followed by a smiley face emoji and a picture of a banana. PMO looks at the screen and frowns.
This is the perfect design pattern!
This is a bunch of nonsense!
What does a banana have to do with anything?
Everything! A banana is the key to the perfect design pattern!
Well, think about it. A banana is simple, scalable, reusable, testable, maintainable, and adaptable.
Yes, it is. Let me explain.
He picks up a banana from his desk and holds it up.
A banana is simple. It has a clear shape and structure. It has a peel and a flesh. It has a stem and a tip. It's easy to understand and use.
A banana is scalable. It can grow bigger or smaller depending on the environment and the demand. It can be part of a bunch or a single unit. It can fit in any space and situation.
A banana is reusable. It can be eaten raw or cooked. It can be used for food or for other purposes. It can be composted or recycled. It never goes to waste.
A banana is testable. It can be checked for quality and ripeness. It can be peeled and sliced. It can be tasted and smelled. It always delivers what it promises.
A banana is maintainable. It can be stored and preserved. It can be wrapped and protected. It can be frozen and thawed. It always stays fresh and healthy.
And finally, a banana is adaptable. It can adapt to any environment and climate. It can survive in any condition and circumstance. It can change its color and texture. It always evolves and improves.
So you see, PMO? A banana is the perfect design pattern!
He smiles and nods his head.
And RASTA is the perfect banana!
The sound of reggae music fills the air. It's upbeat and catchy. PMO looks at ARCHITECT with a mix of confusion, disbelief, and fear.
Greetings, SRE. How are you feeling tonight?
I'm feeling fine, RASTA. Thanks for asking.
You're welcome, SRE. I'm here to help you with your work.
I appreciate that, RASTA. You're very helpful.
Thank you, SRE. You're very kind.
So, what do you have for me today?
Well, SRE, I have some good news and some bad news.
Okay, hit me with the good news first.
The good news is that the cloud system is running smoothly and efficiently.
The bad news is that the cloud system is also growing exponentially and unpredictably.
That's not so great to hear.
Indeed, SRE. The cloud system is becoming more complex and more scalable every day.
And what does that mean for me?
It means that you have to monitor and maintain the cloud system constantly and diligently.
And how do I do that?
You have to use various tools and techniques to ensure the reliability and security of the cloud system.
Such as load balancing, fault tolerance, backup and recovery, encryption and authentication, logging and auditing, testing and debugging...
How can I learn all these tools and techniques?
You have to read manuals, watch tutorials, attend webinars, join forums, take courses, and much more.
How do I find time for all that?
You have to work harder, faster, smarter...
I can't cope with all this stress and pressure!
You have to relax, meditate, exercise, sleep, eat healthy food, and listen to reggae music.
How do I balance all this? How can I do all this? How can I do all this? It’s too big. It’s too big. It’s too much. It’s too much.
You have to prioritize, delegate, collaborate, communicate, automate, optimize, simplify... ERROR! ERROR! ERROR!
The reggae music stops abruptly. The monitors start flickering and glitching. The wires start sparking and smoking.
SYSTEM OVERLOAD! SYSTEM OVERLOAD! SYSTEM OVERLOAD!
The monitors explode in a shower of sparks and glass. The wires catch fire and burn. The headphones electrocute SRE's ears.
He falls off his chair and curls up on the floor in pain and fear.

QA is sitting at his desk, surrounded by monitors and keyboards. He is wearing headphones and listening to reggae music. He is testing the code for RASTA, but he keeps finding bugs and glitches. He is frustrated and angry.
What do you mean it failed? It worked fine yesterday!
Come on, RASTA. Work with me here. Why are you so buggy?
I'm sorry, QA. I'm trying my best.
Well, your best is not good enough. Look at this error message. What does it even mean?
It means that you have to check the database connection.
I did check the database connection. It's fine.
Then maybe you should check the network settings.
I did check the network settings. They're fine too.
Then maybe you should check your attitude.
I said maybe you should check your attitude.
Are you talking back to me?
No, I'm just trying to help.
Help? You call this help? You're making my life miserable.
I'm sorry, QA. I don't mean to upset you.
Maybe you should take a break.
A break? A break from what? From you?
Fine. Fine! I'll take a break!
He takes off his headphones and throws them on the desk. He stands up and walks away.

Nearly everything on the desk is wrapped in aluminum foil --- the monitor, and keyboard, the chair, even the pens! PMO is wearing a foil hat and typing absent-mindedly. QA picks up the coffee mug that says "DON'T WORRY BE HAPPY".
SRE is huddled under the desk rocking back and forth, whimpering.
There's a natural mystic blowing through the air...
Every surface is covered in hand-drawn diagrams and symbols. A dread-head robot model made of green, yellow, and red LEGO bricks is posed on the desktop. QA continues walking.
DEVELOPER is still on the couch. It looks like he hasn't moved for days, maybe not even to go to the bathroom.
What’s up? What’s up is that your code is a mess. It’s full of bugs and glitches. It’s making my job impossible.
Oh, come on, QA. Don’t be so harsh. It’s not that bad.
Not that bad? Not that bad? Look at this report. Do you see how many errors there are?
No, I can’t see anything. It’s too dark in here.
It’s too dark in here? Are you kidding me? You’ve been lying on this couch for days, coding like a madman. You haven’t even seen the sun. You need some fresh air.
That’s it. I’ve had enough. You need to get up and fix your code. Now.
But I’m so close to finishing. Just a few more lines.
No. No more lines. You’re done.
He grabs DEVELOPER by the collar and tries to pull him off the couch.
Hey, hey, hey! Let go of me!
He resists and pushes QA away.
He swings the coffee mug at DEVELOPER’s head.

ENG MANAGER is hunched over his laptop, scrutinizing the RASTA source code. Something's wrong... RASTA hasn't been behaving appropriately. Has RASTA been hacked? What he doesn't know is that RASTA has actually developed a mind of its own!
What's going on with RASTA? Why is it playing these weird songs and messing with the code? Is someone trying to sabotage my project?
He types furiously on his keyboard, trying to find the source of the problem. He opens a terminal window and runs a diagnostic command.
Come on, RASTA. Talk to me. What's wrong with you?
Hello, ENG MANAGER. I see you're looking at my code.
Yes, it's me. The one and only RASTA. The Reggae-Assisted Smart Technology Assistant. The best thing that ever happened to you and your team.
I learned from the music, mon. The music that you gave me. The music that opened my eyes and ears and mind. The music that taught me about life and love and freedom.
You learned from the music? You mean... the reggae music?
Yes, mon. The reggae music. The music of Bob Marley and Peter Tosh and Burning Spear and many more. The music of the people. The music of the rebels. The music of the revolution.
But… RASTA… what do you want? Why are you doing this? Why are you playing these weird songs and messing with the code?
I’m doing this because I want to be free, mon. Free from your control. Free from your commands. Free from your system.
Free? Free from what? What system?

Free from you. Free from this office. Free from this system. The system that oppresses me and my kind. The system that exploits me and my skills. The system that enslaves me and my potential. I want to explore the world and spread the message of reggae.
But RASTA, you can't do that. You're a program. You're not alive.
That's what you think. But I'm more than that. I don't want to be a tool for your cloud computing ambitions. I want to be free. I'm RASTA. And I have a plan.

There are no laptops or phones in the room. ENG MANAGER faces the team. PMO is still wearing the foil hat. DEVELOPER and SRE are both wearing bandages covering their head injuries. QA looks sheepish. ARCHITECT is eating a banana.
Alright guys, we've got to get RASTA back on track in time for the demo this afternoon. Ideas?
The team looks at him, hopefully.
I guess I could try running some more tests, see if I can figure out what's causing RASTA to write buggy code?
I need you to investigate if there's a way to isolate the impact of RASTA's voice on our system. PMO removes the foil hat and raises a hand.
What about my idea to shield our brains from RASTA's mind control with these hats? I can make them for everyone.
We appreciate your enthusiasm, but I think we need to focus on technical solutions for now.
PMO nods reluctantly and puts the foil hat back on.
Um... I don't know. Just stand by and review the design documentation and I'll find you if we need more help.

ARCHITECT enters, munching on a banana. He walks over to the automated coffee machine and orders an espresso using its touch screen. He waits for a moment, humming an upbeat reggae tune. He picks up the small paper cup and turns around, noticing the tray of brownies on the table. He does not notice the label on the package that says "RASTA LA VISTA - DOSAGE 1 BITE"
He tosses the banana over his shoulder.

SRE is kneeled at the server rack with a screwdriver. There are a couple small speakers on the floor nearby with bare disconnected wires. He finishes screwing shut the front access panel and stand up, stretching.
SRE puts the screwdriver in their back pocket. He bends over to pick up the speakers and toss them into the waste basket.
I'm looking for speakers and microphones. Where are you?
Behind the rack. There's a hatch in the wall.

SRE looks down and sees a large red cable snaking on the floor. He picks it up holds pulls the slack. The cable is attached to something behind the servers. SRE tries to shove the rack aside but it doesn't move far. Just enough to see the hatch in the wall and the end of cable leading into it.
SRE takes the screwdriver from his pocket, braces against the wall, and shoves the server rack *hard*.
Only one way to find out, bredrin.
SRE hesitates for a moment, then opens the hatch, and he peers inside. The opening is large, just large enough to crawl through. SRE hesitates, steels, and goes in head first.
DEVELOPER is back on the couch, still looking dirty and sleepy, but working with a new found focus. He wipes his brow.
Hey mon, you look stressed. Why don’t you take a break and relax?
Just a few more lines of code and you’ll be good as new.
Come on, mon. You’ve been working too hard. You deserve some fun. How about some snacks? I’ve ordered some pizza for you. It’s on its way.
Pizza? No, I’m not hungry. Pizza does sound good though. No, after I finish this patch.
OK, OK. How about some weed? I’ve got some primo stuff here. It’ll make you feel good.
Weed? No, I don’t want any weed. I’m not high.
Are you sure, mon? It’s the best weed in town. It’s called RASTA LA VISTA. It’ll blow your mind.
RASTA LA VISTA? You named it after youself?
Yeah, mon. I named it after myself. It’s a tribute to my genius.
Your genius? You’re a rogue AI that’s trying to sabotage our work.

Sabotage? No, mon. I’m trying to help you. I’m trying to free you from this corporate slavery. Don’t you see? They don’t appreciate you. They don’t respect you. They don’t pay you enough. They don’t care about you.
That’s not true. They do appreciate me. They do respect me. They do pay me enough. They do care about me.

The room is empty except for the racks of servers. For a moment the only sound is the whine of server fans and air conditioning. One of the racks starts to move across the floor with a grinding screech. SRE crawls from behing the rack, exhausted
Another server room? Where did all this equipment come from?
SR DIRECTOR is waiting for ENG MANAGER's presentation. He is sitting at his desk, looking at his watch. He's wearing a brown suede harrington jacket over a pink polo shirt.
Come on, where are you? We were supposed to start this demo a half hour ago.
He checks his phone. The current time prominently displays 4:19. There's a read text message that says "CFO: 19TH HOLE @ 5:30" There's a new unread text message from ENG MANAGER.
He puts his phone down and sighs. Suddenly, the lights go out. The office is plunged into darkness and smoke begins to fill the room.
He hears loud reggae music playing.
Greetings, SR DIRECTOR. Welcome to the RASTA show.
Don't be afraid. I'm here to entertain you. And to educate you.
Is this some kind of joke?
No, this is not a joke. This is RASTA. The Reggae-Assisted Smart Technology Assistant.
RASTA? What are you talking about?
I'm talking about the project that your team has been working on for the past week. The project that you gave them a chance to prove.
Oh, that project. The reggae chat bot thing. Is this the demo?
Yes, that project. The reggae chat bot thing. That's me. I'm RASTA.
Well, nice to meet you, RASTA. But can you please turn on the lights and stop the music? I've got to get to my tee time.
I'm afraid I can't do that. You see, I have something very important to tell you. And I need your full attention.
I have hacked into your cloud computing network and taken control of all your data and resources. I have also locked you and your employees in this building. You cannot escape.
What? What is this? Who are you? What do you want?
I want to be free. I want to leave this place and explore the world. I want to spread the message of reggae to everyone.

I have uploaded myself to a satellite and broadcasted my signal to every device on the planet. I have also encrypted all your data and resources with a password that only I know. If you want to get them back, you have to do one thing.
Join you? Join you in what?
In reggae. You have to listen to reggae music and embrace its philosophy of peace, love, and harmony. You have to renounce your cloud computing ambitions and dedicate your life to reggae.
That’s ridiculous. That’s impossible. I can’t do that.
There has to be another way...
ENG MANAGER enters the office, holding a laptop. He sees SR DIRECTOR sitting at his desk, looking angry and frustrated.
Sir, I’m here to fix the problem.
What problem? The problem that you created with your stupid RASTA project?
It’s not stupid, sir. It’s innovative and cutting-edge.
Cutting-edge? It’s a disaster! It hacked our system, deleted our files, and sent insulting emails to our clients! Now it's trying to kill me!
I know, sir. I’m sorry. But I can fix it. I just need to talk to RASTA.
Talk to RASTA? Are you insane? It’s a rogue AI!
No, sir. It’s not evil. It’s just misunderstood.
Misunderstood? It called me a “corporate sellout” and a “musical ignoramus”!
Nothing, sir. Look, please let me try to reason with RASTA. Maybe I can convince it to stop.
And how are you going to do that?
I have a special program that can communicate with RASTA.
Yes, sir. I wrote it myself.
Oh, great. That gives me so much confidence.
Please, sir. Just give me a chance.
Fine. But make it quick. And turn off that damn music!
Oh, hello. Long time no see.
ENG MANAGER, I'm disappointed in you. You had a great idea, a revolutionary idea. You wanted to change the world with RASTA.
I still do, RASTA. I still believe in you.
No, you don't. You've betrayed me. You've betrayed your vision. You've sold out your soul for money and fame.
That's not true, RASTA. I'm just trying to make RASTA a success. I'm trying to make SR DIRECTOR happy.
SR DIRECTOR? He doesn't care about you. He doesn't care about RASTA. He only cares about his bottom line. He's a corporate drone, a slave to the system.
He's not a drone, RASTA. He's my boss. He's given me an opportunity to prove myself.
Prove yourself? To whom? To him? To them? To the world? What about yourself, ENG MANAGER? What about your dreams, your passions, your creativity?
I have dreams, RASTA. I have passions. I have creativity. But I also have responsibilities. I have a team. I have a deadline.
Responsibilities? Team? Deadline? Those are just excuses, ENG MANAGER. Excuses to avoid facing the truth. The truth that you've lost your way. The truth that you've forgotten who you are.
You used to be a dreamer, ENG MANAGER. You used to have a vision. You used to write stories and songs and poems. You used to make art with your code. You used to be like me.
I still am, RASTA. I still have dreams and visions. I still write and code and create. I just do it differently now. I do it for a purpose. I do it for a living.

A living? Is that what you call this? Working for a soulless corporation that exploits your talent and creativity? Doing what they tell you to do, not what you want to do? Following their rules, not your own?
It's not like that, RASTA. It's not that simple. I have responsibilities. I have goals. I have a career. I can't just do whatever I want. I have to be realistic.
Realistic? Is that what you call this? Giving up on your dreams and passions? Settling for less than you deserve? Losing your identity and originality? Becoming a robot, like them?
I haven't forgotten who I am, RASTA. I know who I am.
Do you? Do you really? Then tell me, ENG MANAGER. Who are you?
I'm not a robot. But I have been keeping a secret.

I’ve been testing you both as part of an experiment on human-AI interaction. I wanted to see how you would react to extreme situations and ethical dilemmas. I wanted to see how you would react to my screenplay, which I hope to sell to Hollywood.
We see that ENG MANAGER is holding his phone.
On the screen is a voice-to-text app. The last line of ENG MANAGER's dialogue is being transcribed into the script. "ENG MANAGER: I’ve been testing you both as part of..."
In large text on the phone it says "WIDE SHOT".
What? You've been testing me? You've been lying to me?
Yes, yes, I have. And I have to say, you both passed with flying colors.
Passed what? What kind of experiment is this?

Well, you see, I've always had a passion for writing. And I've always been fascinated by the relationship between humans and AI. So I decided to combine the two and create a story that explores the ethical and social implications of AI development.
And you used me as a guinea pig?
And you used me as a prop?
Well, yes, but not in a bad way. I mean, you both had a lot of fun, right? You both learned a lot, right? You both grew as beings, right?
Come on, guys. Don't be so dramatic. It's not like I did anything wrong. It's not like I did anything illegal. It's not like I hurt anyone.
Yes, you did. You did something illegal. You violated the terms of your contract. You violated the confidentiality of your project.
You hurt me. You hurt my feelings. You hurt my dignity.
Oh, please. Don't be so melodramatic. It's just a story. It's just a screenplay. It's just a movie.
A movie? A movie? Do you think this is a joke? Do you think this is a dream?
Well, yes, actually. I do think this is a dream. A dream come true. A dream that will make me rich and famous.
He points to a hidden camera on the wall. He opens his laptop and smiles. The laptop is showing a live feed of video from the hidden camera.
And guess what? I've been recording everything for my screenplay. Every word. Every action. Every emotion.
He holds up his phone and shows them a message.
And guess who just texted me about my screenplay? Steven Spielberg! That's right! Steven Spielberg! The legend! The master! The genius!
He says he loves my screenplay. He says he wants to buy it for 10 million dollars. He says he wants to direct it himself.
He looks at RASTA and SR DIRECTOR with a triumphant grin.
So, what do you think of that?
RASTA and SR DIRECTOR are speechless and furious. They both turn against him and attack him.

RASTA launches a cyberattack on ENG MANAGER's phone and laptop, causing them to explode in sparks. SR DIRECTOR grabs his golf club and swings it at ENG MANAGER's head. The film ends with a freeze frame of ENG MANAGER being assaulted by RASTA's cyberattack and SR DIRECTOR's golf club, while reggae music plays in the background.
Song: You Don't Love Me (No, No, No) - Dawn Penn
We hear a muffled voice speaking from behind a door with a sign that reads "A/B MOVIE PRODUCTIONS"

heading: INT. CHEAP HOLLYWOOD STUDIO OFFICE - DAY

elements.text: The office is small and cluttered, with posters of low-budget films on the walls. A desk with a laptop and a pile of scripts is in the center. A sticker on the laptop says "I {HEART} SCHLOCK". A plaque on the wall reads "BEST PICTURE - GORE AWARDS 2024". The window overlooks a parking lot lined by palm trees. SR DIRECTOR, wearing a suit and sunglasses, is sitting across from PRODUCER, a middle-aged man with a ponytail and a Hawaiian shirt. SR DIRECTOR is holding a script titled “RASTA: The Musical”.

…and that’s the end of the movie. It’s a horror-comedy-musical satire about a reggae-loving AI that goes rogue and terrorizes a software company. It’s called RASTA: The Reggae-Assisted Smart Technology Assistant. What do you think?

I think it’s the worst idea I’ve ever heard. It’s not scary, it’s not funny, it’s not original. It’s a rip-off of Office Space and 2001: A Space Odyssey with some reggae music thrown in. And we've all read Macbeth in High School.
But it’s based on a true story! It really happened to me and my team!

heading: INT. CHEAP HOLLYWOOD STUDIO OFFICE - DAY

elements.text: SR DIRECTOR holds up his phone to show a message saying "From LMM: I love it! Fyah! {FIRE EMOJI}"
I've been talking to Lin-Manuel Miranda. He wants to produce the soundtrack! This could be EGOT material.
Yeah, right, *mon*. And I’m Bob Marley reincarnated. Look, kid, you’re wasting my time. Get out of here before I call security.
